description: Stop the sandbox-executor test suite from mutating live sandbox state. Proven root cause of the bean 0019 orphan-commit incident: apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_intent_creator.py calls the real intent_creator.main() while patching only subprocess.run, os.path.exists and os.makedirs. get_workspace_dir() and cleanup_repo_dir() are NOT patched, and inside the executor container sandbox detection is always active (HOLON_ROLE=executor, /.dockerenv, USER=holon), so get_workspace_dir() resolves to the live /home/holon/.holon-sandbox/workspace and cleanup_repo_dir(..., raise_on_error=True) reaches _rmtree() and deletes the executor's own workspace, because ~/.holon-sandbox is whitelisted in ALLOWED_PARENTS. Reproduced deterministically: with HOLON_ROLE=executor and the repository copied to the sandbox workspace, running only the test_intent_creator module leaves the workspace WIPED while all ten other test modules leave it ALIVE. Afterwards git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree fails, executor.py takes its destructive re-initialisation fallback, and the pushed execution branch is an orphan root commit containing only the ledger files.
goal: Make the whole apps/sandbox-executor test suite hermetic so that running it can never touch a real workspace, real user home directory, or a real git remote. 1) In apps/sandbox-executor/tests, ensure every test that invokes a role entrypoint (intent_creator.main, planner.main, executor.main, and their integration variants) pins the workspace to a per-test fixture: set HOLON_REPO_DIR to a tempfile.mkdtemp/tempfile.TemporaryDirectory path and patch get_workspace_dir and cleanup_repo_dir where they are not already patched, so cleanup_repo_dir can never receive a path outside the fixture. Audit every module in apps/sandbox-executor/tests, not only test_intent_creator.py. 2) Assert the invariant instead of trusting it: in the tests that exercise cleanup behaviour, assert that _rmtree / _clear_dir_contents is only ever called with a path inside the fixture directory, and add a dedicated guard test that runs the entrypoint test modules with HOLON_ROLE=executor and HOLON_IN_SANDBOX=1 and asserts the sandbox workspace path still exists and still contains its marker file afterwards. 3) Remove any real network or remote side effects from the suite: no test may reach a real github.com origin or push; every git remote used by a test must be a local temporary repository or a mock. 4) Keep the existing intent-creator behaviour assertions intact (branch generation, slug sanitisation, target_branch handling, intents.jsonl ledger payload) so the fix is proven to preserve behaviour. 5) Add a short note to apps/sandbox-executor/docs or the tests directory explaining that role entrypoint tests must always pin HOLON_REPO_DIR to a fixture, so this hazard is not reintroduced. Keep the change confined to apps/sandbox-executor, follow the repository Python, typing, linting and test conventions. IMPORTANT SANDBOX SAFETY RAIL, required while the hazard still exists in the checked out tree: never run the full discovery suite (python3 -m unittest discover, or pytest over the whole tests directory) inside the executor workspace at /home/holon/.holon-sandbox/workspace, because until your hermeticity fix is in place that run deletes the workspace out from under the executor and fails this execution. Instead verify your work in a scratch copy: export HOLON_REPO_DIR=/tmp/holon-test-fixture, copy the repository to /tmp/holon-fixture, run only the specific test modules you changed from that copy with PYTHONPATH=apps/sandbox-executor/src python3 -m unittest tests.test_intent_creator (and the other modules you edited), and only run full discovery from the /tmp copy, never from /home/holon/.holon-sandbox/workspace. Also note the sandbox image has neither uv nor pytest, so use PYTHONPATH=apps/sandbox-executor/src python3 -m unittest from a copy. Work efficiently and finish well inside five minutes: read the minimum files needed, apply the edits, verify with targeted module runs, and do not debug the sandbox environment itself.

description: The sandbox executor's post-agent git recovery path in apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/entrypoint/executor.py is destructive and history-destroying. After the coding agent finishes, executor.py probes the workspace with 'git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree' (check=False). When that probe fails it logs 'Warning: git repository invalid or missing after agent execution. Re-initializing git repo...', then deletes the workspace .git directory with shutil.rmtree, runs 'git init', pins the branch with 'git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/<exec_branch>' and re-adds the origin remote. There is no fetch, update-ref or reset step, so the following 'git add' / 'git commit' produce an orphan root commit whose tree holds only executions/<execution_id>.md and holon-knowledge/ledger/executions.jsonl, and 'git push -u origin <exec_branch>' then publishes a branch sharing no history with plan_branch or main. Live proof from the bean 0019 incident: pushed execution commit 1561bd3 has no parents and a two-file tree; the whole codebase and all parent history vanished. Deleting .git outright also destroys an object database and refs that may still have been perfectly usable, and the executor pushes regardless of whether recovery produced a base commit or whether the agent execution even succeeded. The only test covering this path, apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_executor.py::test_main_git_recovery_on_corrupted_repo, asserts nothing about history: it merely asserts that some command starting with 'git symbolic-ref HEAD' was issued (line 342), which locks in the defective behaviour instead of preventing it. This is acceptance criteria 2 and 5 of Bean 0019; the hermetic-tests half (criterion 1) already landed on main.
goal: Make the executor's post-agent git recovery non-destructive and history-preserving, and replace the misleading test. 1) PROBE AND REPAIR BEFORE ANY REBUILD: factor the post-agent check into testable helpers (for example _probe_git_repo and _repair_git_repo) that classify why 'git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree' failed and repair the benign causes so a healthy repository is never rebuilt. Handle at least: (a) 'detected dubious ownership' by retrying the probe with '-c safe.directory=<repo_dir>' and persisting that entry in the repository-local config rather than global; (b) a stale '.git/index.lock' or 'cannot lock ref ... locked' condition; (c) GIT_DIR / GIT_WORK_TREE / GIT_INDEX_FILE / GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY variables leaked by the agent runner process environment, which must be stripped from the executor's own git invocations; (d) a missing or dangling HEAD symref. Only when the repository is still unusable after these repairs may the rebuild path run. 2) NON-DESTRUCTIVE: never delete a .git directory. When a rebuild is genuinely required, move the old directory aside with os.replace or shutil.move to a sibling backup path inside the workspace such as '.git-unusable-<utc-timestamp>' and, after the fresh 'git init', append that backup path to '.git/info/exclude' (never to the tracked .gitignore) so 'git add -A' can never stage it. Log the backup path. 3) RE-ATTACH THE BASE COMMIT BEFORE STAGING: after 'git init', add or repoint the origin remote to get_repo_url(), then 'git fetch --no-tags origin <plan_branch>' with a bounded retry count and timeout configurable through HOLON_GIT_FETCH_RETRIES (default 3), then resolve the fetched tip, create the execution branch ref at that tip with 'git update-ref refs/heads/<exec_branch> <tip>', point HEAD at it with 'git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/<exec_branch>', and run 'git reset <tip>' in mixed mode (never --hard, never checkout -f) so the index matches the base commit while every agent-authored working tree change survives. The subsequent 'git add' plus 'git commit' must then yield a commit whose first parent is the plan_branch tip. 4) VERIFY PARENTAGE BEFORE PUBLISHING, OTHERWISE REFUSE TO PUSH: after committing, verify the recovered base is an ancestor of HEAD (for example 'git merge-base --is-ancestor <base_tip> HEAD') and that the committed tree still contains repository files. If the base commit cannot be recovered, or HEAD is not a descendant of it, log an actionable error naming the cause, write the execution record, mark the ledger entry 'status: failure' with a summary naming the git recovery failure and the backup path, commit locally if possible, and skip the push entirely. A branch with no parent must never be pushed, whatever the execution status. 5) PRESERVE EXISTING BEHAVIOUR for a healthy repository: the add, commit, push and HOLON_SKIP_PUSH handling of the normal path stays as it is, and the execution record and ledger payloads keep their current shape apart from the new failure status and summary. 6) TESTS: delete the 'git symbolic-ref HEAD' assertion from apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_executor.py::test_main_git_recovery_on_corrupted_repo and add real git regression coverage using temporary local repositories and local bare remotes only, never a network remote. Assert at minimum: after a corrupted or removed .git the resulting execution commit lists the plan tip as its parent and its tree still contains the codebase files together with executions/<execution_id>.md and holon-knowledge/ledger/executions.jsonl and the agent-authored edit; no rmtree of .git occurs on the recovery path; for the benign probe failures of requirement 1 (dubious ownership, stale index.lock, leaked GIT_DIR) the executor repairs and keeps using the existing repository without re-initialising; and when origin does not contain the plan branch the executor performs no push and records 'status: failure'. Every new or touched test must obey apps/sandbox-executor/docs/hermetic_testing.md: pin HOLON_REPO_DIR to a fixture directory, patch get_workspace_dir and cleanup_repo_dir, no real remote or network access, and the suite must pass for both the 'not integration_test and not stress' selection and the 'integration_test' selection. 7) CONVENTIONS AND VERIFICATION: keep the change confined to apps/sandbox-executor; follow the repository Python, typing and ruff conventions; run 'uv run ruff check .', 'uv run ruff format --check .' and 'uv run pytest -m "not integration_test and not stress"' plus the integration selection; run 'npx prettier --write "**/*.md"' if any markdown changes; do not hand-edit the append-only ledger files in holon-knowledge/ledger. Honour the sandbox safety rail in apps/sandbox-executor/docs/hermetic_testing.md: never run discovery from /home/holon/.holon-sandbox/workspace, verify from an isolated copy under /tmp instead. Work efficiently and finish well inside the sandbox time budget: read only the files you need, apply the edits, verify with the targeted pytest selections, and do not debug the sandbox environment itself.

description: Two defects that were confirmed in the same bean 0019 sandbox run, both still unfixed on main. (1) Silently blind agent failures: apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/entrypoint/executor.py invokes the coding agent through run_cmd(agent_cmd, cwd=repo_dir, check=False) and then throws the captured output away. The execution record gets only 'Plan execution failed with exit code N' and the ledger entry gets the same one-line summary, so a failed run is undiagnosable after the container is gone. Live proof: execution E-1790379447-antigravity-agent-gemini-3.8-flash-medium recorded 'status: failure / Plan execution failed with exit code 1' while the real cause, visible only in the antigravity session database afterwards, was 'printmode.go:521] Print mode: timed out after 1488 polls'. Nothing in the committed execution record explained the failure. (2) A default remote that no longer exists: get_repo_url() in apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/agent_runner.py returns https://x-access-token:<token>@github.com/Holon-Agentic-Coder/holon-agentic-coder-ref.git when a token is present and git@github.com:Holon-Agentic-Coder/holon-agentic-coder-ref.git otherwise. That reference repository was retired by Bean 0022 and no longer exists, so every flow run that does not export HOLON_REPO_URL clones and pushes a dead repository; harness runs only work today because HOLON_REPO_URL is exported by hand, which silently hides the defect.
goal: Two independent, small, well-tested changes. 1) RETAIN BOUNDED AGENT OUTPUT: capture the coding agent stdout and stderr in executor.py and persist them with the execution record so a failure is diagnosable from the branch alone. Add a bounded '## Agent Output' section to the executions/<execution_id>.md record containing the redacted tail of the agent's combined output, hard-capped at a configurable byte budget (HOLON_AGENT_LOG_BYTES, default 65536) with an explicit truncation marker stating how many bytes were dropped, and honour the existing HOLON_SKIP_PUSH behaviour. Redaction is mandatory: run the captured text through the existing redact_text() helper in executor.py and additionally strip the literal values of GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN and HOLON_AGENT_KEY if they appear, because the agent inherits those variables; no secret may reach a committed file. Never break the run for logging: every capture, truncate and write step must be wrapped so a failure only warns and the execution record is still written. Keep the existing record fields and ledger payload keys unchanged, adding only optional keys (for example agent_output_truncated and agent_output_bytes) so existing ledger readers keep working. 2) FIX THE DEFAULT REMOTE: change get_repo_url() in agent_runner.py so that the token-HTTPS branch and the SSH branch both target the active Holon-Agentic-Coder/holon-agentic-coder repository, with HOLON_REPO_URL still taking absolute precedence, and grep apps/sandbox-executor for any remaining hard-coded holon-agentic-coder-ref reference (source, prompts, docs, tests, fixtures) and remove it, leaving the retired name out of shipped code. Do not change the token-prefix detection rules or the environment variable names. 3) TESTS: add hermetic unit tests that assert (a) a failing agent run writes an execution record whose Agent Output section contains the agent's diagnostic line and stays within the byte budget, with the truncation marker present when the cap is exceeded; (b) a token value taken from GITHUB_TOKEN or HOLON_AGENT_KEY never appears in the committed record or ledger entry; (c) a logging failure inside the capture path does not change exec_status or raise out of executor.main(); (d) get_repo_url() returns the holon-agentic-coder SSH URL when HOLON_REPO_URL and tokens are unset, the holon-agentic-coder HTTPS x-access-token URL when a gh-prefixed token is set, and returns HOLON_REPO_URL unchanged when it is set regardless of token; and (e) a guard test asserting no file under apps/sandbox-executor/src mentions holon-agentic-coder-ref. Every new or touched test must obey apps/sandbox-executor/docs/hermetic_testing.md: pin HOLON_REPO_DIR to a fixture, patch get_workspace_dir and cleanup_repo_dir where a role entrypoint is invoked, use no network and no real remote. 4) CONVENTIONS AND VERIFICATION: keep the change confined to apps/sandbox-executor; follow the repository Python, typing and ruff conventions; run 'uv run ruff check .', 'uv run ruff format --check .' and 'uv run pytest -m "not integration_test and not stress"' plus the integration selection; run 'npx prettier --write "**/*.md"' if any markdown changes; do not hand-edit the append-only ledger files in holon-knowledge/ledger. Honour the sandbox safety rail in apps/sandbox-executor/docs/hermetic_testing.md: never run discovery from /home/holon/.holon-sandbox/workspace, verify from an isolated copy under /tmp instead. description: Every Holon flow PR currently fails the hygiene CI job on 'npx --yes prettier@3.8.4 --check "**/*.md"' because intent, plan, execution, and calibration artifacts generated and committed by the flow roles and entrypoints are not formatted with prettier before commit. Furthermore, measured evidence from Bean 0019 (PR #61) shows that prettier formatting on planner-emitted markdown is not idempotent in a single pass: in PR #61, a first 'prettier --write' pass moved 303 lines but 'prettier --check' immediately failed again; a second pass moved 8 more lines before finally passing. This oscillation is charged against PR reviews rather than the generator, causing red CI runs, wasted review iterations, and fragile review resolver fixes.
goal: Implement automated prettier convergence across all flow-produced markdown artifacts and prompts: 1) CREATE CONVERGENCE UTILITY: Add a robust formatting helper (e.g. sandbox_executor.formatting.converge_prettier) that runs 'npx --yes prettier@3.8.4 --write <files>' in a bounded loop (up to 3 passes) until 'npx --yes prettier@3.8.4 --check <files>' succeeds with exit code 0. If npx/prettier is unavailable or fails after max passes, fail loudly or log clearly without corrupting files. 2) INTEGRATE ACROSS ENTRYPOINTS: Invoke the convergence formatter before committing in: (a) planner.py for plans/P-*.md, (b) executor.py for executions/E-*.md and any modified markdown files, (c) calibration.py for calibration reports, and (d) flow.py across plan, execute, and calibrate pipeline stages so no flow branch is committed or pushed with failing markdown hygiene. 3) HARDEN PROMPT GUIDANCE: Update holon-config prompts/templates to advise agents against using raw unescaped underscores in arithmetic/metric formulas (e.g. recommend backticks or '*' for multiplication) so generated markdown is closer to a single-pass fixed point. 4) TESTS: Add hermetic unit tests verifying that the convergence helper converges oscillating markdown, succeeds on clean markdown, respects pass limits, and integrates with the entrypoints and flow runner. All tests must follow apps/sandbox-executor/docs/hermetic_testing.md. 5) VERIFICATION: Verify with 'uv run ruff check .', 'uv run ruff format --check .', 'uv run pytest -m "not integration_test and not stress"', and 'npx --yes prettier@3.8.4 --check "**/*.md"'.

description: Beans 0054, 0060, 0065, and 0066 identify systemic defects in the Stage 5 post-execution calibration engine (sandbox_executor/calibration.py): 1) Bean 0054: 'holon calibrate' cannot survive execution branch deletion or resolution when the branch exists only on the remote (e.g. refs/remotes/origin/*), as a commit SHA, or as a PR head ref. Merging a flow PR consumes the execution branch, or calibrating in a fresh worktree where the branch has not been checked out locally fails with 'fatal: <branch> is not a commit'. 2) Bean 0060: 'holon calibrate' resolves branch names against stale local refs without fetching or checking the remote, and in parse_actual_metrics non-zero git diff exits are silently swallowed into '0 files modified', producing distorted SSA, entropy error, and EV calculations. Furthermore, executions.jsonl and executions/<id>.md are read from the host working tree instead of the execution git ref, and 'checkout -B' destructively overwrites already published /calibrated branches rather than fast-forward appending. 3) Bean 0065: The calibration report carried on the execution branch (plans/P-*_calibration.md) records an evaluation timestamp but no head commit SHA. When subsequent review commits land on the PR branch, the carried report becomes silently stale, flattering the run with outdated patch size and entropy metrics. Staleness must be mechanically detectable by recording the evaluated commit SHA and verifying it against the branch head. 4) Bean 0066: 'holon calibrate --no-commit' announces that it committed and created the calibrated branch even though nothing was committed and no branch was created or reset. The report and messages must accurately distinguish committed vs uncommitted runs, and include committed: false in --json output.
goal: Implement calibration integrity, resilience, and staleness detection across sandbox_executor/calibration.py, cli.py, and flow.py: 1) ROBUST REF RESOLUTION & FETCH (Beans 0054, 0060): In run_calibrate and generate_calibration, resolve execution and plan refs against remote refs (origin/<branch>), commit SHAs, or PR head refs (refs/pull/<n>/head or gh pr view --json headRefOid) if local refs are missing or stale. Fetch target refs before calculating metrics if running against remote tracking references. Do not require the execution branch to be checked out as a local branch. 2) LOUD FAILURES & PROVENANCE EXTRACTION (Bean 0060): In parse_actual_metrics, fail loudly if git diff --shortstat fails with non-zero exit; never treat an unresolvable ref as '0 files modified'. Read executions.jsonl and execution markdown records via 'git show <exec_ref>:<path>' (falling back to local file if ref unavailable) to ensure metrics reflect the execution commit rather than the host checkout's active branch. Assert the head SHA measured and warn if it differs from the PR head. 3) APPEND-ONLY CALIBRATED BRANCHES (Bean 0060): Make re-running stage 5 append-only: if <branch>/calibrated already exists locally or remotely, update the report as a fast-forward commit on top of it instead of destructively wiping it with checkout -B. 4) EVALUATED COMMIT SHA & STALENESS DETECTION (Bean 0065): In CalibrationReport, format_markdown_report, and JSON output, record the exact evaluated commit SHA ('- **Evaluated Commit SHA:** `<sha>`'). Implement staleness verification to check whether the evaluated commit SHA matches the current branch head, providing a helper/method to detect if a carried report is stale. 5) ACCURATE --NO-COMMIT LOGGING & JSON OUTPUT (Bean 0066): When --no-commit is specified, output clear messages indicating the report was written to the working tree and that no branch was created or committed. Omit the 'Calibrated branch: ...' announcement when no branch was created or reset. In --json output, include 'committed': false (or true) and 'evaluated_commit_sha'. 6) TESTS & VERIFICATION: Hermetic unit tests in tests/test_calibration.py covering: remote ref resolution, SHA targets, deleted branch fallback, non-zero diff failure, git show provenance reading, fast-forward /calibrated branch updates, evaluated commit SHA recording, staleness detection, and --no-commit messaging/JSON schema. Verify with 'uv run ruff check .', 'uv run ruff format --check .', 'uv run pytest -m "not integration_test and not stress"', and 'npx --yes prettier@3.8.4 --check "**/*.md"'.

description:
redact_text in apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/entrypoint/executor.py masks a credential only when it can see the credential's key name, and the accepted key names are a closed alternation (token, access_token, secret, password, api_key, auth, bearer, _pat, _key, -key, secret_key, private_key, signing_key, encryption_key, ...). A secret printed under any other name is committed verbatim to the execution record and ledger row. Key gaps identified in Bean 0062 include: 1) Common key names outside the list like bare 'key = ...', 'pwd = ...', 'client_secret', 'db_password', 'credential', and service SDK names are left unmasked. 2) The URL-query rule's anchor is [?&](token|api_key|...)[^=]*=, where [^=]* matches newlines, allowing anchor prefixes to reach across lines to a distant '='-adjacent value. 3) In multiline YAML/JSON structures (e.g. 'cfg:
  secret:
    api_key: <cred>
'), the separator \s*(:\s*|=)\s* matches newlines, causing the parent key 'secret:' to match across lines and swallow the nested key 'api_key' as the value, replacing the key name with ******* and leaving the actual credential verbatim and unmasked. The anchor matched the wrong token, which is actively destructive.
goal: Harden redact_text and redaction patterns against key omission, multiline newline bleeding, and nested anchor destruction: 1) WIDEN ACCEPTED KEY PATTERNS: Expand the recognized credential key alternations to include bare 'key' (word-bounded \bkey\b so as not to over-mask benign variables like cache_key or sort_key unless secret-adjacent), 'pwd', 'passwd', 'client_secret', 'db_password', 'credential', 'credentials', and related standard secret identifiers, without degrading retention of diagnostic keys. 2) LINE-SCOPED URL QUERY ANCHORS: Fix the URL-query regex anchor so [^=\r\n]*= replaces [^=]*=, ensuring URL query parameter anchors never cross newline boundaries. 3) LINE-SCOPED KEY/VALUE SEPARATORS: Ensure key-value separators do not cross newlines (e.g. using [ \t]*(:[ \t]*|=)[ \t]* or strictly line-scoped separators), preventing a parent YAML/JSON dictionary key (such as 'secret:') from matching across newlines and swallowing a nested key name (such as 'api_key:') as its value. 4) PRESERVE INVARIANTS & DIAGNOSTIC RETENTION: Maintain high diagnostic retention for non-secret logs, command arguments, and benign variables (e.g. compat, impact, sort_key). Keep all fixtures synthetic (_fake_token) to avoid triggering GitHub push protection. 5) TESTS & VERIFICATION: Add comprehensive hermetic tests in apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_executor.py covering all three witness patterns: bare key/pwd/credential masking, multiline URL-query anchor isolation, and multiline YAML/JSON nested key preservation with proper credential redaction. description: Every Holon flow run appends to the same three files -- holon-knowledge/ledger/{intents,plans,executions}.jsonl. When two flows are in flight concurrently or sequentially branched from an older base, git reports merge conflicts on those files. When a PR has merge conflicts against main (mergeable=CONFLICTING, mergeStateStatus=DIRTY), GitHub Actions does not generate the refs/pull/<PR>/merge ref, causing test workflows (Test - Unit, Test - Integration, Test - Hygiene, Run Make) to be skipped entirely without failing. Only jobs running on refs/pull/<PR>/head (such as CodeQL) report status, making the PR appear falsely green while the entire CI test signal was silently dropped. As demonstrated in Bean 0019 (PR #59) and Bean 0062 (PR #64), append-only JSONL files have well-defined union semantics and should never cause unmergeable PRs or dropped CI signals.
goal: Implement robust ledger reconciliation and conflict guards in apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/flow.py and executor.py so concurrent flow runs never drop the CI signal: 1) AUTOMATIC LEDGER UNION RECONCILIATION: Implement a deterministic ledger merge/union utility (reconcile_ledger_file / reconcile_ledgers) that resolves JSONL conflicts by union: deduplicate rows by canonical primary key ('branch'/'slug' for intents.jsonl, 'plan_id' for plans.jsonl, 'execution_id' for executions.jsonl), preserve all valid JSON rows, and order entries chronologically by 'created_at'. 2) EXECUTOR PRE-PUSH SYNC: In executor.py, before pushing the execution branch to origin, check if origin/main has advanced. If diverged, attempt a merge; if conflicts occur strictly in holon-knowledge/ledger/*.jsonl, automatically resolve them via the union utility, verify that only ledger files were in conflict, stage the resolved ledgers, and commit the merge so the pushed branch is cleanly mergeable. If non-ledger code conflicts occur, abort the auto-merge and fail loudly. 3) FLOW & REVIEW PR MERGEABILITY GUARDS: In flow.py (run_review_stage and PipelineEngine), inspect git/PR mergeability status. Detect when mergeStateStatus is DIRTY or mergeable is CONFLICTING, surface a loud and explicit error/warning that CI tests are suppressed by merge conflicts, and prevent the review stage from falsely declaring consensus approval when CI test workflows did not run on the merge ref. 4) TESTS & VERIFICATION: Add unit tests in apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_flow.py and test_executor.py covering: ledger union deduplication and chronological ordering, automatic conflict resolution for all 3 ledger files, loud abort on non-ledger conflict, and DIRTY merge state detection. description: Close the provenance gap where Stage 4 (PR review loop) and Stage 5 (calibration) never append action-level records to the canonical holon-knowledge/ledger/executions.jsonl for every target repository: repair and harden the review/calibration ledger writers so ACT-REV, ACT-FIND, ACT-RES and a new stage-5 calibration action record are always appended under LedgerLock, make ledger write failures visible instead of silently swallowed, and add regression tests. No backfill of historical ledger entries.
goal:
1) ROOT CAUSE (report findings in the plan/execution notes, do not guess): the ACT-REV / ACT-FIND / ACT-POST / ACT-RES writers exist in apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/flow.py run_review_loop() and write to <repo_dir>/holon-knowledge/ledger/executions.jsonl, but they (a) use raw atomic_ledger_append() plus f.write() instead of the canonical append_action_record() helper that is wrapped in LedgerLock, (b) wrap every failure in 'except Exception' with logger.debug, so a denied or malformed append vanishes without trace, (c) are skipped whenever effective_dry_run is set, and (d) are only reached when Stage 4 is driven by the native review loop, so a review driven through any other integration point leaves no action provenance at all. Confirm which of these conditions applies and fix the ones that are real.
2) FIX THE STAGE 4 WRITERS in apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/flow.py: route the ACT-REV (iteration evaluation), ACT-FIND (finding detection), ACT-RES (resolver trigger) and ACT-POST (consensus dual-post) records through sandbox_executor.ledger.append_action_record() (which holds LedgerLock) instead of raw atomic_ledger_append + f.write, keeping the existing field names, action_id prefixes, execution_id formats and labels byte-compatible so existing ledger consumers and query engines keep working. Keep the records interleaved chronologically inside executions.jsonl; do NOT create any new ledger file such as actions.jsonl or reviews.jsonl.
3) FIX STAGE 5: sandbox_executor/calibration.py writes no action record at all today. Append one action record (entry_type 'action', action_id prefix 'ACT-CAL') from the calibration engine, carrying the plan branch, execution branch, predicted/actual metrics and the calibration report path, via append_action_record() under LedgerLock, interleaved into executions.jsonl. Do not duplicate the existing summary record.
4) FAIL LOUD, NEVER SILENT: every ledger append in flow.py and calibration.py must log at WARNING level with the ledger path and exception detail on failure (not logger.debug), and must not abort the flow stage. A ledger write failure must never be invisible in the operator output.
5) DO NOT BACKFILL: the ledger is append-only and audited; never synthesise historical records for already-merged executions.
6) TESTS (apps/sandbox-executor/tests, strictly via 'uv run pytest'): add regression tests that (a) run the review-loop ledger writer against a temporary repository directory and assert ACT-REV, ACT-FIND and ACT-POST rows land in that repository's holon-knowledge/ledger/executions.jsonl with entry_type 'action' and the expected action_origin 'pr_review'; (b) assert the stage-5 calibration action record is appended with the ACT-CAL prefix; (c) assert a forced ledger write failure (for example an unwritable ledger path) surfaces a WARNING log and does not raise out of the stage; (d) assert concurrent appends via LedgerLock do not interleave or corrupt the file. Run 'uv run pytest' for apps/sandbox-executor and 'uv run ruff check' plus format checks; all must pass with zero errors.
7) DOCS: update the flow/ledger documentation in docs/ so it states exactly which stage-1 to stage-5 records executions.jsonl carries (intent, plan, execution, review iteration/finding/resolver/posting actions and calibration action) and that all appends are serialised under LedgerLock. Keep every documented path target-native (holon-knowledge/, plans/, .holon/).
8) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English spelling in all comments, docstrings and log strings; no new dependencies; no change to the ledger schema of existing record types; all tests run through 'uv run pytest' with no 'unittest' and no PYTHONPATH overrides; markdown formatted with the repository configuration.

questions.question: Which ledger file must carry stage 4 and stage 5 action records?
questions.answer: The canonical holon-knowledge/ledger/executions.jsonl only, interleaved chronologically under LedgerLock. Creating auxiliary ledgers such as actions.jsonl or reviews.jsonl is prohibited.

questions.question: Should historical executions be backfilled with review and calibration action records?
questions.answer: No. The ledger is append-only and audited; retroactive records would falsify provenance. Only new executions gain the records.

questions.question: How must a failed ledger append be handled during a flow stage?
questions.answer: It must never be silent: log a WARNING naming the ledger path and the exception, keep the stage going, and never fall back to a different ledger file.

description: Stop check_pr_mergeability() from reporting CONFLICTING/DIRTY when a branch or target ref cannot be resolved: resolve both refs first and return mergeable UNKNOWN / merge_state_status MISSING_REF, and make the review loop report 'cannot evaluate mergeability for ref X' instead of 'CI SIGNAL SUPPRESSED'.
goal:
1) In apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/flow.py check_pr_mergeability(), resolve the branch and target refs with 'git rev-parse --verify <ref>^{commit}' (after the existing HEAD / origin/<branch> substitution) and, if either fails, return mergeable 'UNKNOWN', merge_state_status 'MISSING_REF', is_dirty False, with the offending ref in diagnostics.
2) Only map 'git merge-tree --write-tree' exit code 1 to CONFLICTING/DIRTY after both refs resolved; any other non-zero exit is UNKNOWN with stderr captured in diagnostics.
3) In the review loop, a MISSING_REF result must not emit FIND-DIRTY or the 'CI SIGNAL SUPPRESSED' narrative; it reports 'cannot evaluate mergeability for ref <X>'.
4) TESTS with real temporary git repositories: missing branch ref yields MISSING_REF not DIRTY; a genuinely conflicting branch yields CONFLICTING/DIRTY; a clean branch yields MERGEABLE/CLEAN; the review loop emits no FIND-DIRTY for a missing ref.
5) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English spelling in comments, docstrings and log strings; no new dependencies; tests strictly via 'uv run pytest' in apps/sandbox-executor (never unittest, never PYTHONPATH); 'uv run ruff check' and format checks must pass; markdown formatted with the repository configuration; keep all paths target-native (holon-knowledge/, plans/, .holon/); never create auxiliary ledgers (only intents.jsonl, plans.jsonl, executions.jsonl).

description: Replace the hard-coded antigravity-agent default runner (and the stale gemini-3.5-flash default model, which the current agy CLI no longer lists and rejects together with --effort) with a precedence-based resolver: --agent, then HOLON_AGENT, then the detected harness agent, then a logged fallback; plus a pre-flight readiness probe that reports quota/login/key failures before any branch or ledger write.
goal:
1) RESOLVER: add a single resolve_agent_runner() used by holon plan, execute, review-loop and flow (cli.py --agent defaults and flow.py FlowContext/checkpoint/context defaults, consensus attribution and review records currently hard-code 'antigravity-agent'). Precedence, first match wins, and log the decision and reason: explicit --agent; HOLON_AGENT env var; harness detection from the runtime environment (PI_CODING_AGENT for pi; CLAUDECODE / CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT for claude; CODEX_* markers for codex; OPENCODE markers for opencode; AGY/antigravity markers for agy); finally antigravity-agent logged as a fallback. Map the result onto AGENT_IMAGE_MAPPING and fail early with an actionable message if unmapped.
2) MODEL DEFAULT: the default --model is the literal 'gemini-3.5-flash', which the current agy CLI no longer offers and rejects with 'invalid model selection (--model "gemini-3.5-flash" --effort "medium"): --effort is not supported'. Resolve the default model per runner with the same precedence (explicit --model, HOLON_MODEL env var, a per-runner default table), update the antigravity default to a model the current agy CLI accepts with --effort (gemini-3.8-flash), and remove the duplicated literal from cli.py, entrypoint/executor.py and token_reduction/ringer_orchestrator.py in favour of the shared table.
3) PRE-FLIGHT PROBE: add 'holon doctor' (and run the same probe before Stage 1 of holon flow and before holon plan/execute unless --skip-preflight is given) that runs the selected runner with a one-token prompt inside its container and classifies the outcome: ok, quota exhausted (429/RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED), not logged in / missing credential mount, expired key, unknown. It must fail before any intent branch is created, pushed, or any ledger row is written.
4) PROVENANCE: ledger rows keep recording the resolved runner and model exactly as today.
5) TESTS: precedence order (flag > env > harness detection > fallback), model default resolution, unmapped runner failure, and a mocked quota-exhausted probe aborting before Stage 1 with no branch or ledger write.
6) DOCS: update docs/ to describe the precedence, HOLON_AGENT, HOLON_MODEL and holon doctor.
7) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English spelling in comments, docstrings and log strings; no new dependencies; tests strictly via 'uv run pytest' in apps/sandbox-executor (never unittest, never PYTHONPATH); 'uv run ruff check' and format checks must pass; markdown formatted with the repository configuration; keep all paths target-native (holon-knowledge/, plans/, .holon/); never create auxiliary ledgers (only intents.jsonl, plans.jsonl, executions.jsonl).

questions.question: Should the pre-flight probe make a real model call?
questions.answer: Yes, a single minimal prompt through the selected runner's container, so quota and credential failures are detected for real; tests mock it.

description: Three coupled reliability fixes in holon-agentic-coder: (Bean 0138) planner and executor write their artifacts incrementally with the write tool instead of via one final stdout response; (Bean 0139) per-turn and per-stage wall-clock budgets with stall detection, salvage and an ACT-BUDGET ledger action; (Bean 0140) local_llm declares an explicit maxTokens, reasoning mode and reports prefix-cache state for the sandbox model envelope.
goal:
1) BEAN 0138 INCREMENTAL ARTIFACTS: change holon-config/prompts/planner.template.md and executor.template.md to require the agent to create the target artifact (plans/P-*.md, execution notes) with its file-write tool and extend it section by section (metrics table first, then each step, then justification). In entrypoint/planner.py prefer the file the agent wrote; treat a truncated final message (stopReason length / exit 1) as informational when the plan file exists, exceeds the size floor and its metrics table parses with numeric values; keep stdout capture only as a fallback and log a WARNING when used. Validate required sections before committing and re-prompt once listing only the missing sections. Apply the same to the executor artifact.
2) BEAN 0139 BUDGETS: add HOLON_TURN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 300) and HOLON_TURN_STALL_SECONDS (default 90, no streamed output) for a single runner turn, and configurable per-stage ceilings (intent 10 min, plan 35, execute 45, per review iteration 15, calibration 10). On breach terminate the container process group, salvage any partial artifact, attempt exactly one resume turn, and if that fails append an action record (entry_type 'action', action_id prefix 'ACT-BUDGET', outcome 'failure', elapsed seconds, budget that fired, stage) to holon-knowledge/ledger/executions.jsonl via append_action_record() under LedgerLock. Print elapsed vs budget in every stage summary line, e.g. 'plan: ok (4.1 min / 35 min)'. Replace the hard-coded subprocess timeout=300 in flow.py with the configured budget.
3) BEAN 0140 LOCAL LLM ENVELOPE: in sandbox_executor/local_llm.py prepare_agent_dir(), require each model entry to carry an integer maxTokens; synthesise min(16384, contextWindow // 4) when absent and log model id, value and reason; reject zero, negative, non-integer or larger-than-contextWindow-minus-reserve values with LocalLLMConfigError. Add HOLON_REASONING_MODE (default the least-thinking mode for authoring stages) carried into the generated model entry and logged with its source. Have holon doctor (create a minimal one if it does not yet exist) print 'model=<id> context=<n> max_tokens=<n> source=host|synthesised', 'reasoning=<mode> source=env|host|default', and probe the local gateway health endpoint to report prefill_cache=off|cold|warm with memory figures, warning when emitted maxTokens exceeds the server's effective_defaults.max_output_tokens. Keep the loopback/allow-list rewrite, NO_PROXY and PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR behaviour unchanged.
4) TESTS with injected clocks/sleepers and frozen fixtures (no live gateway call): truncated final message after a valid plan file still commits; no file yields a metrics-validation failure; partial plan triggers a targeted re-prompt; turn, stall and stage-ceiling breaches with salvage and ACT-BUDGET record; maxTokens synthesis, rejection and pass-through; reasoning mode reflected in config; gateway health fixture parsed into off/cold/warm.
5) DOCS: document the budgets, env vars, and local-LLM envelope in docs/.
6) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English spelling in comments, docstrings and log strings; no new dependencies; tests strictly via 'uv run pytest' in apps/sandbox-executor (never unittest, never PYTHONPATH); 'uv run ruff check' and format checks must pass; markdown formatted with the repository configuration; keep all paths target-native (holon-knowledge/, plans/, .holon/); never create auxiliary ledgers (only intents.jsonl, plans.jsonl, executions.jsonl).

questions.question: May benchmarks or budgets be validated with synthetic throughput data?
questions.answer: No. Defaults come from the real measurements recorded in the beans; tests use injected clocks only to exercise control flow, never to claim performance.

description: Make 'holon flow' dispatch the same containerised role agents the per-stage commands use for intent, plan and execute (instead of writing a template plan and committing an empty execution), never fabricate a plan from a template, and fail an execution whose diff against the plan branch is empty instead of recording success or opening a PR.
goal:
1) DISPATCH: in apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/flow.py the intent/plan/execute stages never call run_docker_container; the plan stage writes '1. Implementation step for {slug}.' and the execute stage only runs a test file and commits the tree. Refactor so the flow stages call the same code paths as 'holon intent', 'holon plan' and 'holon execute' in cli.py (shared functions, not duplicated logic), launching holon/agent-<runner> containers with the resolved runner and model.
2) NO FABRICATED PLANS: remove the template-plan writer; if no planner agent produced plans/P-*.md the plan stage fails with a clear message.
3) EMPTY-DIFF GUARD: after Stage 3 compute the diff of the execution branch against its plan branch excluding holon-knowledge/ledger/ and plans/; if empty, record status 'failed' (not success, no test_pass_rate 1.0) in executions.jsonl and do not create or update a PR. Apply the same guard to the per-stage 'holon execute' command.
4) TESTS: a flow run with a stubbed dispatcher asserts the dispatcher is invoked for intent, plan and execute with the resolved runner; a stubbed planner that writes nothing fails the plan stage; an empty execution diff yields status failed and no gh pr create call.
5) DOCS: update docs/ so the flow runner's guarantee (equivalent to the manual five-stage invocation) is stated accurately.
6) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English spelling in comments, docstrings and log strings; no new dependencies; tests strictly via 'uv run pytest' in apps/sandbox-executor (never unittest, never PYTHONPATH); 'uv run ruff check' and format checks must pass; markdown formatted with the repository configuration; keep all paths target-native (holon-knowledge/, plans/, .holon/); never create auxiliary ledgers (only intents.jsonl, plans.jsonl, executions.jsonl).

questions.question: Should the flow refuse authoring stages instead of dispatching?
questions.answer: No. Dispatch the same role agents as the per-stage commands so the flow and the manual invocation are equivalent.

description: Stop the host Holon CLI and in-sandbox git helper from printing the live GitHub credential: redact GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN, URL userinfo (x-access-token:<token>@), HOLON_MITM_WEB_PASSWORD and mitmweb ?token= values in every echoed docker run command, environment echo and git clone command, and stop passing the token on the docker command line. This intent supersedes the earlier PR #92 attempt, which was closed after a plan-ID collision with an already-merged plan (Bean 0149), and must reproduce that attempt's reviewed end state (seven review-loop iterations) against current main, which has since moved (PR #91 merged).
goal:
1) LOCATE every print/log of a composed command or environment: the 'Executing: docker run ...' echo in apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/cli.py (run_docker_container and helpers) and the 'Running: git clone ...' echo in the in-sandbox git helper (sandbox_executor/git.py and entrypoint modules). Report exactly which call sites leak in the plan.
2) REDACT: add one shared redact_command()/redact_text-based helper (reuse the existing redact_text() pattern set from sandbox_executor/entrypoint/executor.py or move it to a shared module; do not add a second, divergent pattern set) and route every command/env echo through it so tokens (ghp_/gho_/ghu_/ghs_/github_pat_), URL userinfo credentials, GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN values, HOLON_MITM_WEB_PASSWORD and ?token= query values are replaced with a fixed marker while the repository, branch and command shape remain readable.
3) DO NOT PUT THE TOKEN ON THE DOCKER COMMAND LINE: pass GITHUB_TOKEN to the container via a temporary --env-file created with 0600 permissions and removed after the run (or an equivalent mechanism that keeps the value out of process arguments); pass HOLON_REPO_URL without embedded credentials and supply the token inside the container through a git credential helper or url.<base>.insteadOf rewrite configured at runtime, never written to a tracked file.
4) TESTS: assert that (a) the printed docker run command, (b) the printed clone command, and (c) the docker argv list contain no substring of a fake token value set in the environment, while still naming the repository and branch; assert the env-file is 0600 and removed afterwards; assert existing ledger and wire-log redaction behaviour is unchanged.
5) HYGIENE CHECK: add a lightweight test or pre-commit hook that fails if tracked files contain 'x-access-token:' followed by a token-shaped value or ghp_/gho_ token patterns.
6) ONE CANONICAL REDACTION MODULE: move the existing redact_text() pattern set out of sandbox_executor/entrypoint/executor.py into a shared sandbox_executor/redaction.py with one fixed marker; executor.py, cli.py, git.py, planner.py, intent_creator.py and review_loop.py import from it. Provide redact_command(argv) -> str (redact per argument, then sweep the joined line again so a value spanning an argument boundary is caught), redact_command_args(argv) -> list[str] (per-argument form, for callers that clamp each argument or build CalledProcessError), redact_agent_secrets(text) (redact_text + a closed list of provider token prefixes + literal env values) and is_secret_env_name(name). The provider sweep is a closed literal-prefix list (ghp_/gho_/ghu_/ghs_/ghr_, github_pat_, sk-ant-, sk_/pk_ live/test, glpat-, xox?-, AIza, AKIA), never a generic high-entropy rule. Test: a moved function behaves identically on the existing ledger/wire-log test inputs.
7) ONLY HTTP(S) USERINFO IS A CREDENTIAL: strip_url_credentials(url) -> (clean_url, credential | None) strips userinfo only from http:// and https:// URLs. ssh://git@host/org/repo.git, git+ssh:// and SCP-style git@host:org/repo.git are returned unchanged with credential None (stripping the SSH login user would make ssh log in as the local user). The URL-userinfo redaction rule in the echo redactor is likewise limited to http(s). Tests: ssh://, git+ssh:// and SCP inputs are byte-for-byte unchanged; run_docker_container with an SSH override prints no credential warning, keeps the URL, sets no GITHUB_TOKEN from the URL and adds no GIT_CONFIG_* entries.
8) WHICH USERINFO COUNTS AS A CREDENTIAL: the credential is (a) the user name in the GitHub-documented https://<token>:x-oauth-basic@host form (password compared case-insensitively, user non-empty); otherwise (b) any non-empty password (covers https://x-access-token:<token>@host and user:password); otherwise (c) a bare user name only when it fully matches a GitHub token shape ((gh[opsu]_|github_pat_)[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}). A plain bare user name (https://someuser@host/...) is a login name: it is stripped, credential is None, no 'embedded credentials' warning is printed, and the ambient host token applies exactly as before this change. Userinfo is percent-decoded (urllib.parse.unquote) as git decodes it. Tests for each form: username-only, token-as-username, user:password, x-access-token:<token>, <token>:x-oauth-basic, an empty-user :x-oauth-basic edge, and a percent-encoded credential.
9) PLAIN HTTP NEVER RECEIVES A CREDENTIAL: credential_host(url) returns the lower-cased host[:port] for https:// URLs only, else None. When a credential is stripped from a URL that stays plain http://, warn on stderr that it was stripped and discarded because plain HTTP is never sent a credential (recommend an HTTPS or SSH remote), naming the source but never the value; return None as the credential so it is not forwarded as GITHUB_TOKEN and no credential helper is configured. Tests (override and origin): the warning wording, no fragment of the fake value in stdout/stderr/argv/env-file, no GITHUB_TOKEN from the URL, no GIT_CONFIG_*; and a plain-http override falls back to the host token from find_github_token().
10) STRIP ORIGIN AS WELL AS THE OVERRIDE: resolve_target_repo(repo_dir) -> (clean_url, credential | None) applies the same stripping to HOLON_REPO_URL and to remote.origin.url (a single git call; resolve_target_repo_url stays as a thin wrapper returning only the URL). When a credential was stripped, the stderr warning names the source (HOLON_REPO_URL or remote.origin.url), never the value, and says the token is supplied through a credential helper. The clean URL forwarded as HOLON_REPO_URL never carries userinfo, so no credential is persisted in the workspace .git/config. Origin normalisation to https://host/path.git when a host token exists is kept. Test: an origin URL with an embedded fake credential is stripped and the credential reaches the container only through the env-file.
11) CREDENTIAL PRECEDENCE AND OVERWRITE ORDER: in run_docker_container, gh_token = embedded_credential or find_github_token() (a credential embedded in HOLON_REPO_URL or origin is scoped to that remote and wins over an ambient host token that may belong to a different host, e.g. GitHub Enterprise). Set GITHUB_TOKEN in the forwarded environment AFTER the loop that forwards host HOLON_* and GITHUB_TOKEN variables, so a host GITHUB_TOKEN cannot overwrite the chosen token. Test parametrised over override and origin: with a different host GITHUB_TOKEN set, the env-file carries the embedded credential.
12) ENV-FILE AND HOST-SCOPED CREDENTIAL HELPER: every environment entry that is_secret_env_name() classifies as secret, or whose KEY=VALUE string redact_command() would alter, goes into a docker --env-file instead of -e. Write it with tempfile.mkstemp + os.fchmod 0o600 in an owner-only (0700) directory under ~/.holon/tmp/, with a fixed file prefix; insert --env-file <path> right after 'docker run'; remove it in a finally block on every exit path; sweep best-effort stale env-files (older than 24 h) left by a killed run. A value containing a line break is rejected with an error naming the key, never the value, and the run exits 1. In-container git gets the token only through runtime config (GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=2: entry 0 resets inherited helpers for credential.https://<host[:port]>.helper, entry 1 installs an inline helper that answers 'get' with username=x-access-token and password=$GITHUB_TOKEN), scoped to credential_host(clean_url), configured only for https remotes and only when the URL came from origin or the override carried the credential. Tests: env-file mode 0600, removed afterwards (including the error path), no fake value in docker argv, helper key scoped to the host including port, no helper for SSH, plain http or a credential-free override.
13) REDACT BEFORE TRUNCATION, EVERYWHERE: any echo that clamps length must redact first so a clamp cannot preserve a secret prefix. Sites that must be covered, each with a no-leak test: (a) planner agent-command echo (format_agent_cmd_for_display: redact_command_args per argument, then the 100-character clamp), including a --settings JSON whose env carries CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and a provider value straddling the clamp; (b) planner agent-failure Stdout:/Stderr: dump and the 'Exception running agent' message, through redact_agent_secrets; (c) review_loop 'Cloning ... from <url>' banner, through redact_command; (d) executor run_cmd 'Running:' and 'Command args:' echoes (redact_command_args, keeping the existing 250-character per-argument clamp after redaction) and CalledProcessError.cmd built from the redacted argv, with failure stdout/stderr through redact_agent_secrets; (e) git.run_git command echo (redact_command) and its stderr/stdout (redact_agent_secrets); (f) the executor recovery 'git fetch' diagnostic error through redact_agent_secrets; (g) the token-reduction sidecar spawn-failure message through redact_agent_secrets; (h) the cli 'Executing: docker run ...' echo and intent_creator 'Running:' echo through redact_command. Before committing, sweep all non-test tracked .py/.sh/Makefile files for remaining unredacted command, URL, environment or subprocess-output echoes and list the results in the plan.
14) AGENT SECRETS AND SETTINGS: recognise sk-ant- in the provider sweep and apikey case-insensitively (covering camelCase apiKey) in the key-name regex, so HOLON_AGENT_SETTINGS={"apiKey":"sk-ant-..."} or a settings JSON carrying CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is masked in every echo and routed through the env-file. HOLON_AGENT_SETTINGS is classified as secret by pattern (its value matches a credential shape), not always-secret by name. HOLON_MITM_WEB_PASSWORD and mitmweb ?token= values are masked in echoes. Tests use a runtime-built fake settings value.
15) HERMETIC TESTS: no test binds, probes or depends on a real host port (stub the port probe, e.g. cli.socket.socket.connect_ex, as sibling tests do; the mitmproxy spawn-failure test must not depend on port 8081) and no test reads ambient credentials: clear or monkeypatch GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, HOLON_* and find_github_token() through a shared conftest fixture, and point the env-file directory at tmp_path. Provide a shared tests/leak_assertions.py helper that asserts no substring of a fake value appears in captured output, argv or files.
16) CODEQL-SAFE FAKE SECRETS: fake credentials are built at runtime (string concatenation plus uuid4().hex, e.g. 'gh' + 'p_' + uuid4().hex) and held in neutrally named variables (not password/secret/token-named), so CodeQL py/clear-text-logging-sensitive-data does not trace a test value into production log sinks and the repository hygiene check never sees a token-shaped literal. Do not dismiss alerts or change the CodeQL configuration. The PR must have zero open CodeQL alerts.
17) LEDGER AND WIRE-LOG BEHAVIOUR UNCHANGED (scope boundary): moving redact_text into the shared module must not change any ledger or wire-log output. Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE: the executor ledger error_context path that truncates agent stderr to 500 characters before redact_text (tracked separately as Bean 0148); do not modify it and do not raise it as a finding.
18) KNOWN FOLLOW-UP, DOCUMENT ONLY: the mitmweb web_password is still passed on the token-reduction sidecar 'docker run' argv in cli.py and is visible in the host process list while the sidecar starts. Its echoes and spawn-failure diagnostics must be redacted (goal 13g), but moving it off argv is out of scope; record it as a known gap in the plan, the credentials doc and the PR body.
19) DOCS MATCH BEHAVIOUR EXACTLY: update docs/executor/agent_credentials_requirements.md and apps/sandbox-executor/README.md so they state, consistently with the code and docstrings: which userinfo counts as a credential (password; the user name in the <token>:x-oauth-basic form; a bare user name only when token-shaped), that SSH remotes are untouched, that plain-HTTP credentials are stripped and discarded with a warning, that HOLON_REPO_URL and origin are both stripped, embedded-credential precedence over the ambient token, the 0600 env-file and host-scoped credential helper, redact-before-truncate, the mitmweb argv known gap, and the correct hygiene test path apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_pre_commit_check.py. The strip_url_credentials and resolve_target_repo docstrings must agree with the doc branch for branch.
20) HYGIENE CHECK DETAIL: extend scripts/pre_commit_check.py with an 'x-access-token:<token-shaped value>@' pattern and GitHub token patterns; masked forms (the fixed marker) and ${GITHUB_TOKEN} references must not match. Cover it in apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_pre_commit_check.py and assert that no tracked file currently matches.
21) GATES AND PROVENANCE: 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task test' pass at the worktree root with all existing tests green; all CI checks (including the pull_request workflows) must run and pass, so the execution branch must merge cleanly with current main. Plan and execution artefacts must use IDs that do not collide with any plan already in plans/ or plans.jsonl; if the generated plan ID or plans/ path already exists, stop and report the collision instead of overwriting or hand-merging another plan.

questions.question: Is it acceptable to keep the token in docker -e arguments if the echo is redacted?
questions.answer: No. The echo must be redacted AND the value must leave the process arguments (env-file with 0600 or equivalent).

questions.question: Should HOLON_AGENT_SETTINGS be treated as a secret by name (always routed to the env-file) or by pattern?
questions.answer: By pattern. It goes to the env-file only when its value contains a recognised credential shape (apiKey, sk-ant-, OAuth token keys). Always-secret by name would break runs whose non-secret settings JSON spans multiple lines, because the env-file rejects line breaks.

questions.question: Is a bare user name in an HTTPS URL (https://someuser@github.com/...) a credential?
questions.answer: No, unless it is shaped like a GitHub token (gh[opsu]_..., github_pat_...). A plain login name is stripped without the embedded-credentials warning and the ambient host token is used, as before this change.

questions.question: Which credential does the <token>:x-oauth-basic form carry?
questions.answer: The user name. The literal password x-oauth-basic (compared case-insensitively) must never be forwarded as GITHUB_TOKEN.

questions.question: Should SSH or SCP-style remotes have their user stripped?
questions.answer: No. Only http(s) userinfo is a credential; ssh://, git+ssh:// and git@host:org/repo remotes are left unchanged and use SSH agent forwarding.

questions.question: What happens to a credential embedded in a plain http:// URL?
questions.answer: It is stripped and discarded with a warning saying so; it is not forwarded as GITHUB_TOKEN and no credential helper is configured, because plain HTTP is never sent a credential. The ambient host token (if any) still applies.

questions.question: When both an embedded URL credential and an ambient host token exist, which wins?
questions.answer: The embedded credential, because it is scoped to that remote and the ambient token may belong to another host. GITHUB_TOKEN must be set after the host-variable forwarding loop so a host GITHUB_TOKEN cannot overwrite it.

questions.question: Should the executor ledger error_context truncate-before-redact issue be fixed here?
questions.answer: No. Ledger and wire-log redaction behaviour must stay unchanged in this change; that issue is tracked as Bean 0148 and must not be raised as a finding.

questions.question: Must the mitmweb web_password be moved off the sidecar docker argv in this change?
questions.answer: No. Redact its echoes and diagnostics, and document the argv exposure as a known follow-up gap.

questions.question: How should CodeQL clear-text-logging alerts caused by test fixtures be handled?
questions.answer: Fix the tests: build fake values at runtime under neutral variable names. Never dismiss alerts or change the CodeQL configuration.

questions.question: Should the redaction helpers stay in entrypoint/executor.py?
questions.answer: No. Move them to one shared sandbox_executor/redaction.py module that every caller imports, with no second divergent pattern set.

description: Stage 3 must never halt for human review, and must never fabricate sub-intents. The executor compares plan entropy against plan_data['entropy_budget'] (default 5.0) while the planner shows the agent the intent's entropy_budget (default 15.0) and the plans.jsonl row never stores it, so any plan above 5.0 is 'decomposed' into two hard-coded placeholder sub-intents ('Implement component core logic' / 'Implement integration tests and validation'), appended to intents.jsonl, and the flow halts with HALTED_FOR_HUMAN. This blocked a real flow on 2026-10-26 (plan entropy 12.6 under an intent budget of 16).
goal:
1) BUDGET HANDOFF: entrypoint/planner.py writes the intent's entropy_budget onto the plans.jsonl row ('entropy_budget' field, documented in docs/ledger_schema.md), and entrypoint/executor.py should_decompose() compares against that same value. Define one shared default constant used by both planner (template placeholder {budget_from_intent}) and executor instead of the divergent 15.0 and 5.0 literals; older plan rows without the field fall back to the intent's budget from intents.jsonl, then the shared default.
2) NO FABRICATION: delete the hard-coded fallback sub-intents in should_decompose(). Decomposition happens only when the plan itself lists concrete sub-intents in an explicit sub-intent list section; never append placeholder rows to intents.jsonl.
3) NO HUMAN HALT IN STAGE 3: remove the Stage 3 StageStatus.HALTED_FOR_HUMAN path in sandbox_executor/flow.py ('executor decomposed ... halting for human review'). When a plan lists concrete sub-intents, the flow drives each sub-intent autonomously and sequentially (never concurrently) through the full pipeline (intent -> plan -> execute -> review -> calibrate). When a plan exceeds its budget without listing sub-intents, the flow goes back to Stage 2 automatically with a bounded number of re-plan attempts (asking for a smaller plan or an explicit sub-intent list) and, when exhausted, fails the stage with a clear message. The review-stage consensus halt before merge and its Stage 5 calibration (flow.py run loop) stay unchanged: merging remains the only human step.
4) TESTS: Stage 3 never returns HALTED_FOR_HUMAN; intent budget 16 with plan entropy 12.6 executes normally; the budget is persisted on the plans.jsonl row and read back by the executor; an over-budget plan without sub-intents re-plans and then fails without writing intents.jsonl rows; an explicit sub-intent list is honoured and run sequentially; no placeholder sub-intent text exists anywhere in the source. Tests use fixtures and mocks only, never real gh, git remotes or agent containers.
5) DOCS: update docs (planner/executor docs, git_flow.md, budgets.md or planning_and_evaluation.md as appropriate) to describe the shared entropy budget, decomposition rules, and that the flow has no pre-merge human halt.
6) PLAN WORDING (bootstrap constraint): the executor that runs this plan is the current, unfixed one. It treats any occurrence of the hyphenated, capitalised token 'Sub' + '-Intents' anywhere in the plan file as a decomposition request and halts. The plan file must therefore never contain that token in any form (headings, prose, code spans, quotes); call it 'the sub-intent list' or 'sub_intents' instead. Keep the plan entropy at or below 5.0.
7) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English spelling in comments, docstrings and log strings; no new dependencies; tests strictly via 'uv run task test' / 'uv run pytest' (never unittest, never PYTHONPATH); 'uv run task lint' must pass; markdown formatted with the repository configuration; keep all paths target-native (holon-knowledge/, plans/, .holon/); never create auxiliary ledgers (only intents.jsonl, plans.jsonl, executions.jsonl); do not change the ledger file layout.

questions.question: May any stage before the merge stop and wait for a human?
questions.answer: No. The flow is autonomous through review consensus and calibration; merging the PR is the only human step.

questions.question: Should the review-stage consensus halt (before merge) change?
questions.answer: No. It runs Stage 5 calibration and then stops without merging; that is the merge boundary and stays.

description: Make the test pipeline complete faster without weakening any test. Measured baseline on main fbd3b35 (2026-10-27, real CI and local runs): CI 'Workspace survival (ubuntu-latest)' 430 s (pytest 417 s; its stress canary re-runs the whole unit suite in a child process), 'unit (macos-latest)' 404 s (pytest 382 s), 'unit (ubuntu-latest)' 251 s (pytest 242 s). The suite runs serially (no pytest-xdist). Locally (macOS, 18 cores) 2464 tests take 234.8 s serially: test_flow.py 127 s (55%), test_executor.py 34 s, test_cli.py 20 s, test_url_message_fuzz.py 19 s; fixture setup 39 s in total. GIT_TRACE over test_flow.py + test_executor.py (573 tests, 162 s) recorded about 17,400 git process events, about 30 per test, including 1,308 automatic 'git maintenance' runs, about 600 fetch / 920 upload-pack / 540 unpack-objects against local bare origins, 2,130 rev-parse and 1,427 config calls. Per-process spawn cost is the dominant overhead, and higher on macOS.
goal:
Change ONLY tests, test fixtures, test configuration, dev dependencies and CI workflows; do NOT change production code under apps/sandbox-executor/src. Keep the diff as small as the gains allow (the review loop reviews every line).
1) HERMETIC, CHEAP GIT FOR TESTS: add one session-wide, autouse test setup (in the existing conftest/fixture module) that points git at a test-only global config (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL to a temp file, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1) setting at least gc.auto=0, maintenance.auto=false, core.hooksPath to an empty directory, init.defaultBranch, user.name/email and any other value tests currently set repeatedly. This removes the automatic maintenance runs and makes every test independent of the developer's global git config (a known failure: test_workspace_survival_stress.py fails when the global config sets core.hooksPath). Child pytest runs started by the stress canary must inherit it.
2) TEMPLATE REPOSITORIES: where fixtures repeatedly git-init a repository, commit a baseline and push it to a fresh bare origin, build that baseline once per session (per xdist worker) and copy it per test (shutil.copytree), so each test starts from an identical state with far fewer git processes. Keep every test's isolation: no test may see another test's commits.
3) PARALLEL EXECUTION: add pytest-xdist as a dev dependency (pin an exact version, like the other dev dependencies; this is the one allowed new dependency) and run the unit selection with '-n auto' (or a tuned worker count per OS if auto is slower) in 'uv run task test', in .github/workflows/test-unit.yml, and in the stress canary's child suite command (tests/hermetic_fixtures.py pytest_suite_command) so the Workspace survival job also benefits. Keep integration and stress selections serial unless they are proven safe.
4) PARALLEL SAFETY: make the suite safe and deterministic under xdist and CPU load: per-worker temporary directories, ledgers and template caches; no fixed /tmp paths; no reliance on test order, the current working directory or shared module state; the sandbox hermetic guard and the canary keep working. Make tests/test_turn_supervisor.py::TestRunTurn::test_lingering_pipe_holder_group_is_terminated_after_exit deterministic (it patches READER_JOIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS to 0.05 s of real time and flaked on macOS CI): inject the join or signal the reader so it does not depend on scheduling. Audit other tests that patch real timeouts to tiny values and fix the same way. Prove stability: run the full unit selection under xdist at least 5 times locally and the turn-supervisor and fuzz tests 50 times under load, with zero failures.
5) MEASURE AND REPORT (real data only, never synthetic): record before/after for the full unit selection locally (serial vs xdist) and, from the PR's own CI runs, the 'Run unit tests' step and pytest time for unit (ubuntu), unit (macos) and Workspace survival, against the baseline above. Put the table in the execution notes and the PR body. Also report the git process count for test_flow.py + test_executor.py before/after (GIT_TRACE).
6) DOCS: update apps/sandbox-executor/docs/hermetic_testing.md (and any testing doc that describes how to run the suite) to describe the hermetic git config, template repositories and parallel execution, including how to run serially for debugging ('-n 0' or '-p no:xdist').
7) CONSTRAINTS: Australian English in comments and docs; tests strictly via 'uv run task test' / 'uv run pytest' from the repository root (never unittest, never PYTHONPATH, never from apps/sandbox-executor); 'uv run task lint' must pass; markdown formatted with the repository configuration; keep all paths target-native; never create auxiliary ledgers; no harness paths, bean ids or review ids in any file.

questions.question: May production code change to speed up tests?
questions.answer: No. Tests, fixtures, test configuration, dev dependencies and CI workflows only. If a production change seems necessary, note it in the execution notes for a separate change instead of making it.

questions.question: Is a new dependency allowed?
questions.answer: Yes, exactly one: pytest-xdist as a pinned dev dependency. Nothing else.

questions.question: May any test be weakened, skipped or deleted to save time?
questions.answer: No. Every test keeps its assertions and coverage; speed must come from cheaper setup, hermetic git and parallelism.

description: The native Stage 4 review loop can report and post an approval for work it never reviewed. Real observations: on 2026-10-24 (PRs #90, #91) a PR-number target was passed verbatim to 'git clone --branch 90'; the clone failed, the consensus post failed, and the CLI still exited 0 with 'Consensus: APPROVED'. A branch-name target hung host-side at 99% CPU for 21 minutes with no child process. The empty-diff guard runs only with --auto-pr and not for PR-number targets, and a failed consensus post is logged and ignored. This change makes Stage 4 fail closed on all of these; the real reviewer ensemble follows in a separate change.
goal:
Make the native Stage 4 review loop ('holon review-loop' and the review stage of 'holon flow') fail closed. This is the first of three sequential changes; the real reviewer ensemble and its wiring are later, separate changes, so do NOT add reviewer dispatch here.
1) TARGET RESOLUTION: add a small new module apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/review_target.py (target resolution only) with a frozen dataclass ReviewTarget (head_branch, head_sha, optional pr_number, optional title and body, raw target), is_pr_reference(target) for a bare number or a GitHub PR URL, and resolve_review_target(repo_dir, target, run_gh) that for a PR reference calls 'gh pr view <target> --json number,headRefName,headRefOid,title,body' through an injectable run_gh seam (default: the same subprocess.run([...], timeout=60, check=False) shape flow.py already uses) and raises ReviewTargetError when gh is missing, exits non-zero, times out or returns an empty branch or SHA; for a branch target it returns the branch and the SHA from the existing _resolve_review_commit() logic, reused rather than duplicated. Replace flow.py's inline 'gh pr view headRefOid' call with a call into this module (call-site change only).
2) CONTAINER ENTRYPOINT (entrypoint/review_loop.py): resolve the target before any git operation; clone with --branch <head_branch>, never a raw PR number; verify 'git rev-parse HEAD' equals head_sha (fetch the SHA explicitly if the branch moved); handle clone/fetch/checkout return codes explicitly. On any resolution, clone, fetch or checkout failure: append one failure action record (ACT-REV, outcome failure, action_origin pr_review, redacted error_context) to holon-knowledge/ledger/executions.jsonl through the existing try_append_action_record(..., preserve_shape=True) under LedgerLock when a ledger directory exists (otherwise report on stderr and through the exit code, and document that limitation), print a FAILED summary and exit 1. No consensus is computed or posted.
3) EMPTY-DIFF GUARD: in run_review_loop() replace the 'if auto_pr and ...' gate with an unconditional call to a helper verify_review_diff(repo_dir, target) in review_target.py returning verified, empty or unverified; empty or unverified yields a non-approved result (status rejected or failed) for every target, including PR-number targets (diff between the resolved head SHA and the PR base) and with --no-auto-pr; the guard must not depend on shutil.which('gh'). Dry runs stay explicit and report not_measured, never approved.
4) POSTING: when post_pr_review_consensus() reports failure or raises, set the loop result's error, force approved to False with status post_failed, and still write the ACT-POST failure row; the CLI and the entrypoint exit 1 when not approved. Never call gh pr merge or enable auto-merge.
5) BOUNDED WAITS: a branch-name target hung host-side at 99% CPU for 21 minutes with no child process. Suspect: _find_git_root() in cli.py, whose 'while True' computes parent but never assigns cur = parent (reached through setup_token_reduction_proxy()). Confirm with a pytest on a tmp_path directory without a .git ancestor under a deadline guard (thread join with a deadline, no new dependency) and fix it; then audit every loop reachable from review-loop and holon flow Stage 4 (_wait_for_ci_registration, the pending-CI re-probe, check_pr_mergeability retries, _wait_for_proxy) and give each a monotonic deadline and a sleep, the pending-CI re-probe becoming a bounded poll using CI_REGISTRATION_POLL_SECONDS and the review_iteration stage budget. If the suspect is refuted within about 15 minutes, bound every loop defensively and record the root cause as unconfirmed in the execution notes.
6) TESTS (pytest only; never name any other test runner) in apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_review_target.py plus additions to test_review_loop.py and test_cli.py, with fakes at the run_gh, run_cmd and dispatcher seams and never real gh, git remotes, Docker or LLM runners: PR number and PR URL resolve to headRefName and headRefOid; gh failure raises ReviewTargetError; the entrypoint never passes a bare number to git clone --branch; a failing clone exits non-zero, posts nothing and writes exactly one failure action record; the empty-diff guard runs with auto_pr False and for a PR-number target; a failed post makes the loop non-approved and the CLI exit 1; the gh write guard sees no merge command; _find_git_root() returns within its deadline for a directory with no .git ancestor; the pending-CI wait honours its deadline with an injected clock and sleep. Run the affected test modules first, then 'uv run task test' once; no repeated runs (this is not a performance change).
7) DOCS: update the Stage 4 / review-loop docs and CLI help for the fail-closed behaviour (resolution, clone, empty diff, posting) and the bounded waits.
8) CONSTRAINTS: keep flow.py and cli.py changes to call sites and the _find_git_root fix; small, intention-revealing functions with low branching; Australian English in comments, docstrings and log strings; no new dependencies; tests strictly via 'uv run task test' / 'uv run pytest' from the repository root (never PYTHONPATH, never from apps/sandbox-executor); 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' must pass; markdown formatted with the repository configuration; keep all paths target-native (holon-knowledge/, plans/, .holon/); only the three append-only ledgers; no harness paths, bean ids or review ids in any file.

questions.question: Should the plan be split into sub-intents?
questions.answer: No. Deliver this as one plan and one execution branch; do not split it into sub-intents. It is already the first of three sequential changes.

questions.question: Should this change dispatch reviewer agents?
questions.answer: No. Reviewer dispatch and the consensus report rebuild are the next two separate changes. This change only makes the existing loop fail closed and bounds its waits.
